title: Fatimah al-Fihri's Qarawiyyin
hook: a woman in Fez spends her inheritance on a mosque that becomes a place of learning

segments.voice: Yesterday: the Moriscos. Granada surrendered, promises broke, and they were forced to convert and then expelled. Your line was: remember the moriscos.

An inheritance arrives. A father has died, and his daughter now has money of her own. A house, a business, a cushion for bad years? In Fez, in Morocco, a woman named Fatimah al-Fihri, whose family had come to the city from Kairouan, the chronicle says, chose a mosque. It would become the Qarawiyyin, and it would not stay only a mosque. The path crosses the strait to North Africa.
screen: `AN INHERITANCE ARRIVES.` → `SHE CHOOSES A MOSQUE.` → `IT WON'T STAY ONLY A MOSQUE.`

segments.voice: Much of the story comes from a later chronicle of Fez, which tells it simply. Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad al-Fihri, was a devout woman. She spent what she inherited on building the mosque, from the ground up. Tradition adds that she fasted the whole time the building went on. And the chronicle says her sister Maryam did the same across the river, building a mosque for the other half of the city. Two sisters, two inheritances, two mosques. Why would someone do this? A hadith fits her story. Sahih Muslim records the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, saying, in substance: when a person dies, their deeds end except for three things. Charity that keeps flowing. Knowledge people go on benefiting from. A good child who prays for them. Fatimah's mosque became the first two at once. Prayer filled it, and then teaching did. Scholars taught the Qur'an, law, grammar, and later much more, and students came from far away to sit in its circles. Over time it grew into what Fez now calls the University of al-Qarawiyyin. So the line isn't an exaggeration, just a long view. Look back over this week, and it's full of builders: a jurist who wrote on love, a judge who defended reason, a mystic, neighbors who built a shared and fragile culture, a palace that credited God with every win, a people who kept faith in hiding. And now a daughter with an inheritance. She founded a university.
screen: `A DAUGHTER'S INHERITANCE.` · `TWO SISTERS, TWO MOSQUES.` · `CHARITY THAT KEEPS FLOWING.` · `FROM PRAYER HALL TO UNIVERSITY.` · then, large: `SHE FOUNDED A UNIVERSITY.`

segments.voice: Bring one woman to mind who started something that outlasted the moment: a grandmother who began a family tradition, a teacher who started a reading club, a neighbor who organized the food drive. Picture what she built, and who is still benefiting from it. If you pray, remember her in your prayer; if you don't, hold her name with thanks.
Qarawiyyin. The mosque Fatimah al-Fihri built in Fez with her inheritance, which grew into a university. Today's word.
Your line: she founded a university. What she began is still flowing. Day nine hundred forty-five, done.

howItsDone: The Qarawiyyin in Fez is still a working mosque and a center of Islamic learning, and Muslims often cite Fatimah al-Fihri as an example of charity that keeps giving.
